one_liner: A Chennai-based fintech that pairs an AI-driven credit-scoring platform (ki score) with a licensed NBFC to extend formal credit to underbanked women and small businesses in India.
recommendation_rationale: The founding team has strong domain pedigree and the NBFC subsidiary reached standalone break-even in February 2025, but the consolidated group is still loss-making and asset quality has weakened sharply in the last reported year. Worth revisiting once the next audited year shows whether the delinquency rise was temporary and whether consolidated losses are narrowing.

snapshot.founded: 2017 (KPL, the holding company); its NBFC subsidiary KCPL was incorporated in March 2021 and began lending in FY23
snapshot.stage: Growth-stage NBFC/fintech (rated CARE BBB-; not a disclosed VC funding stage)
snapshot.total_funding_display: INR 324 Cr cumulative equity raised as of the April 2025 rating report (per CARE Ratings; not independently cross-checked against USD-denominated aggregator totals, which report a materially different figure -- see unresolved gaps)
snapshot.last_round: EUR 5 million (~INR 49 Cr) equity infusion from IDH, Netherlands, in Q4 FY25, per CARE Ratings

business_model: Kaleidofin Private Limited (KPL) owns a data-driven credit-scoring model, ki score, built on a claimed database of 35 million customers and used to underwrite loans.[^1] It monetises this in two ways: a Lending-as-a-Service layer that sells credit assessment (ki score, ki view) and customer-engagement tools to banks, MFIs and NBFCs, and a wholly owned NBFC subsidiary, Kaleidofin Capital Private Limited (KCPL), that lends directly using a branchless, partner-originated model through around 15 originator partners.[^1][^2] KCPL's loan book covers agricultural, women-entrepreneur, micro-entrepreneur and small-business loans.[^1] The company reports serving over 3 million users across 17 states through 50 channel partners, of whom 97% are women and about 1 million run small businesses.[^4]
why_now: KCPL's NBFC arm reached standalone break-even in February 2025 after several years of scaling losses, and its assets under management grew from INR 45 Cr (March 2023) to INR 114 Cr (March 2024) to INR 140 Cr (December 2024).[^1] The group raised roughly INR 156 Cr of fresh equity in FY25 across multiple tranches, lifting tangible net worth to about INR 190 Cr, and in June 2026 KCPL took on its first international impact-debt facility, a USD 5 million four-year Orange Bond-certified debenture from an IIX-backed vehicle, targeting clean-energy and financial-inclusion lending.[^1][^3] In May 2026 the company also closed a KES 276 million agri-finance securitisation in Kenya, its first disclosed move outside India.[^7] Together these suggest a company moving from a single-market NBFC into a multi-market, diversified-funding credit-infrastructure business, though it is unclear from public sources how much management attention and capital this international push is drawing away from the core India franchise.
market_and_competition: Kaleidofin operates in India's underbanked/informal-credit segment, where its stated competition is less about other well-funded fintechs and more about informal-sector alternatives such as chit funds, jewellers and daily deposit schemes; named platform competitors mentioned by one aggregator are FinBox, TransBnk and Linedata.[^6] That aggregator data was retrieved via a search-engine summary rather than a direct page fetch and should be treated as a lower-confidence, unverified secondary source pending direct confirmation.
traction_and_team: On a CARE Ratings consolidated basis, KPL's total income was INR 12 Cr in FY23, INR 29 Cr in FY24, and INR 32 Cr for the first nine months of FY25 (unaudited), against consolidated losses of INR 23 Cr, INR 32 Cr and INR 19 Cr respectively over the same periods.[^1] On a standalone basis, the NBFC subsidiary KCPL was profitable in FY23 and FY24 (small PAT in both years) and reached break-even in February 2025.[^1] Asset quality has weakened: 90+ day delinquency rose from 0.02% as of March 2024 to 1.89% as of December 2024, which CARE Ratings attributes partly to broader stress in the microfinance sector rather than to Kaleidofin specifically.[^1] The leadership team has unusually deep domain pedigree for this segment: CEO Sucharita Mukherjee previously ran credit-derivatives structuring at Morgan Stanley and Deutsche Bank and was founding CEO of Northern Arc Capital, while KCPL CEO Puneet Gupta co-founded the IFMR group (now Northern Arc Capital / Dvara Group) and was on ICICI Bank's founding microfinance team.[^1]

See unresolved_gaps.

years_since_founding.label: years_since_founding
years_since_founding.definition: Years from KPL's stated founding (July 2017, exact day not disclosed; approximated as 2017-07-15) to 2025-04-25, the same date the total_capital_raised figure is measured as of. This is the correct pairing for capital_raised_per_year: measuring 'years since founding' to today instead would understate the true rate, because no capital is assumed to have been raised between the report date and today.
years_since_founding.notes: Exact founding day not disclosed; mid-month approximation used, so this is precise to roughly +/- 2 weeks. Corrected 2026-09-18: an earlier version of this run measured years to the report-generation date instead of to the capital-raised date, understating capital_raised_per_year by about 18%.

claims.text: KPL's total equity capital raised to date is approximately INR 324 crore as of the April 2025 rating report.
KCPL (the NBFC subsidiary) achieved standalone break-even in February 2025.
Kaleidofin was founded in 2017 by Sucharita Mukherjee and Puneet Gupta.
Kaleidofin serves over 3 million users, 97% of whom are women.
Kaleidofin operates across 17 states through 50 channel partners.
KCPL secured a USD 5 million four-year debt facility from an IIX-backed vehicle in June 2026.
Kaleidofin closed a KES 276 million agri-finance securitisation in Kenya in May 2026.
Kaleidofin raised $13.8 million led by Rabo Partnerships in a round reported around September 2024.
Kaleidofin's named platform competitors include FinBox, TransBnk and Linedata; its main competition is informal-sector credit.
Sucharita Mukherjee was previously founding CEO of Northern Arc Capital and worked in credit derivatives at Morgan Stanley and Deutsche Bank.
Puneet Gupta co-founded the IFMR group (now Northern Arc Capital / Dvara Group) and was on ICICI Bank's founding microfinance team.

risks.risk: The consolidated group is still loss-making (INR 32 Cr loss in FY24, INR 19 Cr loss in 9MFY25) even though the NBFC subsidiary reached standalone break-even.
risks.mitigant: Ask management for a consolidated (not just KCPL-standalone) path-to-breakeven timeline and what specifically at the KPL parent level (the ki score licensing business, corporate overhead) is driving the gap.

risks.risk: 90+ day delinquency jumped from 0.02% to 1.89% in nine months, which CARE Ratings partly attributes to sector-wide microfinance stress rather than company-specific issues, but the distinction matters a great deal for underwriting quality.
risks.mitigant: Ask for the most recent delinquency data (post-December 2024), a breakdown by originator partner and geography, and how much of the increase is attributable to ki score-accepted vs ki score-rejected-but-disbursed loans.

risks.risk: The lending business depends on roughly 15 third-party originator partners under a branchless model with first-loss default guarantees (FLDG); concentration in any one partner, or a partner's own financial stress, could disrupt the loan book.
risks.mitigant: Ask for partner-level concentration (percentage of AUM from the top 3-5 partners) and FLDG coverage terms.

risks.risk: No public source disclosed a company valuation, monthly revenue, or a cap table, so standard venture-style metrics (revenue multiple, ARPU, dilution) cannot be computed from public information alone.
risks.mitigant: Request the current cap table, most recent monthly MIS, and the valuation basis of the FY25 equity tranches directly from the company.

what_would_change_recommendation: A move toward Meet would need at least one more audited period showing consolidated (not just standalone-subsidiary) profitability alongside continued AUM growth, plus evidence that the delinquency spike identified in the CARE Ratings report has stabilised or reversed. A move toward Pass would follow from a further deterioration in asset quality, a stalled or down-round equity raise, or evidence that the international expansion is diverting capital from a struggling core business.
founder_questions: What is the plan and timeline to reach consolidated (KPL-level, not just KCPL-standalone) profitability?
What specifically drove 90+ day delinquency from 0.02% in March 2024 to 1.89% in December 2024, and has it stabilised since?
What is the current post-money valuation and cap table following the roughly INR 156 crore raised across FY25?
What share of AUM comes from your largest originator partners, and what happens to the loan book if one of them exits?
How does the Kenya agri-securitisation and the new IIX debt facility fit into capital allocation priorities relative to the core India underbanked-lending business?

rdi_fits.rationale: Kaleidofin's ki score/ki view stack is digital financial-inclusion infrastructure, and its Kenya work is explicitly a digital agri-finance securitisation program. This is a plausible but not confident fit: the RDI Scheme is aimed at private-sector R&D in sunrise/strategic domains, and Kaleidofin's activity here looks more like applied fintech infrastructure deployment than frontier R&D, so eligibility should not be assumed from this theme match alone.

unresolved_gaps: Total capital raised to date is reported very differently across sources: ~INR 324 crore per CARE Ratings (April 2025, audited-adjacent) vs a commonly cited ~USD 42-47 million across aggregator sites (Tracxn/Crunchbase-style, exact figures not independently fetched). These were not reconciled here because doing so would require an unsourced FX-rate and timing assumption; a direct question to the company is the more reliable path.
No public source found in this research pass disclosed a company-level (KPL) valuation for any funding round, which blocks computing a valuation multiple or implied dilution.

No monthly revenue disclosure was found; all revenue figures available are annual or multi-quarter (FY23/FY24/9MFY25 total income), so the standard monthly-based checks (annualised revenue run rate, ARPU, month-over-month growth multiple) could not be computed and correctly show as missing input rather than being estimated.

The Business Standard article on the $13.8M funding round (source 5) could not be directly fetched (HTTP 403); its details rest on a search-engine summary rather than the article's own text, and the competitor list (source 6, Tracxn) is similarly a search-summary of an aggregator rather than a direct fetch. Both should be treated as lower confidence and re-verified before relying on them.

No negative news, regulatory action, customer complaints or litigation involving Kaleidofin specifically were found in this research pass; this is an absence of evidence in the searches run, not confirmation that none exists.
